references.text: The Lord also makes a distinction here between the livestock of Israel and that of Egypt, so that Goshen is protected during the plague of livestock disease.
During the hail plague, Goshen was the only place where it did not hail, demonstrating God's protection over His people.
During the plague of darkness, all the Israelites had light where they lived, while Egypt was in total darkness.
The Lord makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel, so that not even a dog will bark at the Israelites.
Earlier in the chapter, the Lord confirms that there is none like Him, and here He demonstrates this by setting apart Goshen.
Goshen was given to the people of Israel as their dwelling place in Egypt, and it is this area that God now protects.
Israel settled in Goshen and became fruitful there; this is the land that God now protects from the plagues.
The expression 'know that I am the Lord' or similar phrases is repeated here, where God desires that people recognize His power.
Connects God's presence as protection in judgment (Exodus) with the requirement of purity to maintain this presence (Numbers).
A parallel in God's action of 'setting apart' to preserve His people amidst judgment, so that His identity is made known.
Links the historical experience of God's presence in judgment (Exodus) to the eschatological fulfillment where God dwells among His people forever.
Highlights the connection between God's presence as proof of power (Exodus) and as the foundation for an eternal identity without shame (Joel).
A contrasting parallel where God's knowledge is manifested both through protection in judgment (Exodus) and through scattering as judgment (Ezekiel).
